Seminar Title:

Financial Efficiency, Corporate Governance, and Performance of Electricity Distribution Companies in India: Data Envelopment and Panel Regression Analyses

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

School of Management

Speaker Name:

Rajkiran Venkateshgoud Bilolikar

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Conference Hall, SOM, NIT Rourkela

Date and Time:

27 Oct 2026 10 AM

Contact:

Dushyant Mahadik

Abstract:

Despite decades of policy reforms and repeated financial restructuring initiatives, electricity distribution companies (DISCOMs) in India continue to face persistent financial stress. Existing empirical studies and regulatory assessments have predominantly focused on operational and technical efficiency, with relatively limited attention to financial efficiency and its underlying drivers, particularly in the context of state-owned utilities. This study addresses this gap by developing an empirically grounded efficiency framework for Indian electricity distribution companies. Using panel data for 25 state-owned DISCOMs over the period 2015–2022, the study applies a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) model in which key liquidity, leverage, and activity ratios are employed as inputs and Return on Assets (ROA) is used as the output measure of performance. The analytical framework facilitates an assessment of efficiency that is informed by firms’ financial structure and profitability, in addition to operational considerations. Further, panel regression techniques are used to examine the influence of corporate governance mechanisms, including board and audit committee characteristics, on financial efficiency and performance. The results reveal substantial variation in financial efficiency across DISCOMs, with only a small number of utilities operating on the efficiency frontier. Excessive leverage and weak debt-servicing capacity significantly constrain profitability. Corporate governance effects are present but selective, with board and audit committee activity proving more influential than formal board composition. By shifting the analytical focus from operational indicators to financial management, this study offers a new perspective for both researchers and industry demonstrating that utility finances can be examined independently as a source of efficiency improvement and providing a foundation for more targeted, financially driven reform strategies in regulated electricity distribution utilities.
